subject: Does Stan have plans to implement HMC-BFGS?

messages.author: 40b63348dbcb447d
messages.subject: Does Stan have plans to implement HMC-BFGS?
parts:
I mean the sampling algorithm proposed in Quasi-Newton Methods for Markov Chain Monte Carlo. Some threads (1)(2) in the stan-dev group have mentioned the method. So, are there any plans for it? Thanks.

Ziyuan

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Does Stan have plans to implement HMC-BFGS?
parts:
On Sunday, February 10, 2013 4:10:57 PM UTC-5, ZiYuan Lin wrote:
I mean the sampling algorithm proposed in Quasi-Newton Methods for Markov Chain Monte Carlo. Some threads (1)(2) in the stan-dev group have mentioned the method. So, are there any plans for it? Thanks.

I don't think there are any immediate plans to implement that particular algorithm. However, some Stan people (not me) are working on HMC with a non-diagonal mass matrix, either that adapts during the warmup phase and is fixed for the rest of the iterations or is always adapting based on the second and third derivatives of the log-posterior. I'm sure they would be interested if you have a particular case where the implemented diagonal mass matrix methods are not working well.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Does Stan have plans to implement HMC-BFGS?
parts:
I don't have any explicit references, just unpublished experience. In particular, I was using the low-rank metric found in http://arxiv.org/abs/1112.4118, and it became clear that in high dimensions the low-rank approximation cannot fully decorrelate the local neighborhood of the distribution. It's not too surprising, given that the rank stays constant while the dimension increases.

-Mike

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Does Stan have plans to implement HMC-BFGS?
parts: If I remember correctly, in HMC-BFGS the rank of the approximation will end up being ~ the number of samples used to construct the approximation.  That's actually just an upper bound as the rank can be much worse if the set of samples is degenerate (unlikely to happen exactly, but it is likely to be ill conditioned, particularly early in the sampling).
